newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso recovers after initial weakness.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso recovers after initial weakness.

text.p: The Philippine peso rebounded at close, ending at 26.30 to the dollar after early heavy dollar-buying eased up on news that President Fidel Ramos had fully recovered from surgery, traders said.
The peso fell to as low as 26.315 in early morning, down from last Friday's close of 26.301, after news that Ramos underwent an operation earlier in the day to remove an arterial blockage.
Turnover quickly swelled to more than $80 million in less than half an hour of frenzied trading. The Central Bank was quick to intervene, posting its selling rate at 26.315.
By late morning, doctors from the Makati Medical Centre announced that the operation was concluded successfully.
"That's when the market stabilised," one trader said.
The Central Bank did not budge from its selling rate, selling more than $150 million. Total turnover reached $288 million as compared with Friday's $148.4 million.
Some deals were done at 26.325, but the settlements were to be done on Thursday, instead of Tuesday.
"After the panic buying, some banks started selling their overbought dollars back to the market," another trader said.
The weighted average declined to 26.314 from Friday's 26.298.
